_about: Curated argument table of the command explainer (sassi/ui/explain.py; GET /api/explain). Written from the argument definitions of docs/spec/07..11 and docs/spec/00_requirements.md section 3.4, checked against the command handlers (sassi/prep/commands/) and, for record commands, the record FIELDS (names in the same order). Where the specification and the implementation differ, the entry describes the implementation and says so in 'notes'. Schema: {NAME: {summary, configures, source, notes?, args: [{pos, name, meaning, default?, values?, repeat?}]}}.

ACCIN.summary: Names the acceleration input file of spectrum <no> for EQUAKE: a seed record whose Fourier phases are kept (EQUAKE <accopt> = 1) or an external history that is only evaluated (<accopt> = 2).
ACCIN.notes: Used only when EQUAKE <accopt> is 1 or 2 (Error 88 if the file is then blank); the history is in g, first line Δt, then one value per line.

args.name: no
args.meaning: spectrum number, the direction index shared with RSIN, RSOUT, ACCOUT and TPSD (1-3, one per translational direction)

args.name: file
args.meaning: path of the input acceleration history (g); relative paths are searched from the model directory; a blank file name clears the entry

ACCOUT.summary: Names the file that receives the spectrum-compatible acceleration history EQUAKE generates for spectrum <no>; the velocity, displacement, PSD and FFT files reuse its base name (.vel, .dis, .psd, .fft).
ACCOUT.notes: Required for every simulated spectrum (Error 87); the .acc file is in g with Δt on the first line, so it can be used directly as THFILE.

args.name: no
args.meaning: spectrum number (1-3), same index as RSIN, RSOUT, ACCIN and TPSD

args.name: file
args.meaning: path of the generated acceleration history (.acc, in g); a blank file name clears the entry

ACTIVATEPLOT.summary: Makes open plot <id> the active plot, the one that setting commands act on (SASSI-EDU extension; the GUI sends it when a plot tab is brought to the front).

args.name: id
args.meaning: plot number, as printed when the plot opened

ACTM.summary: Makes model number <Model> the active model, on which all later commands act; if no model has that number, an empty model with default analysis settings is created.

args.name: Model
args.meaning: integer model reference number (0 or more)

ADDITION.summary: Creates line <dest> as the sum of the source lines (y = Σ y_i) on the union of their abscissas, like ANSYS POST26 ADD; e.g. summing co-directional histories.
ADDITION.notes: All line math uses the union of the source abscissas with linear interpolation; outside its range a line is held at its first/last value (not zero-padded).

args.name: dest
args.meaning: line number receiving the result (may be one of the sources; an existing line is overwritten)

args.name: source1..source100
args.meaning: line numbers to add (up to 100); an undefined line is an error

ADDRND.summary: Appends random values to a variable until it holds numsamples items, with the RND distributions; the existing items and the counter are kept.

args.name: var
args.meaning: name of the variable to extend (created if undefined)

args.name: numsamples
args.meaning: number of items the variable has AFTER the command (not the number added); nothing is appended if it already has that many

args.name: dist
args.meaning: distribution

values.UNI: uniform real between param1 (minimum) and param2 (maximum)
values.UNIINT: uniform integer in the inclusive range param1..param2 (alias UNINT)
values.NORM: normal: param1 mean, param2 standard deviation
values.LOGNORM: lognormal: param1 mean and param2 standard deviation of the variable itself
values.POISSON: Poisson integer with mean param1 (alias POSSION)

args.name: param1
args.meaning: first parameter: minimum (UNI, UNIINT) or mean (NORM, LOGNORM, POISSON)

args.name: param2
args.meaning: second parameter: maximum (UNI, UNIINT) or standard deviation (NORM, LOGNORM); not used by POISSON

AFWRBAT.summary: Splits the SSI frequency set into <splits> contiguous blocks, each written as a self-contained folder <Model>_<k> with module decks and run scripts, plus combine scripts that join the FILE8 files with COMBIN.
AFWRBAT.notes: Needs MDL; SASSI-EDU writes run_<k>.pre with .sh/.bat launchers (SITE, POINT, HOUSE, FORCE, ANALYS) and combine.pre, which folds the FILE8 files with COMBIN and runs MOTION, STRESS, RELDISP.

args.name: splits
args.meaning: number of frequency blocks (folders), from 1 to the number of frequencies in the SITE frequency set

AFWRITE.summary: Runs CHECK, then writes the input deck <model>.<ext> (.equ, .soi, .sit, .poi, .hou, .frc, .anl, .mot, .str, .rdi, .eql) of every AOPT-enabled module that has no CHECK errors, into the model directory.
AFWRITE.notes: Needs the model name and path (MDL); a module with errors gets no deck and an existing old deck is renamed <deck>.bak (D-AFW-01).

AMP.summary: Appends spectral amplification ratios (SAR = local/reference ATF, one per SSI frequency) for multiple-excitation zone <no>; HOUSE multiplies the free-field motion at that zone's interaction nodes by them.
AMP.notes: Needs HOUSE <me> = 1 (which needs <wpass> = 1); the count must equal the number of frequencies of the set (Error 119); SASSI-EDU keeps zero values after the first one.

args.name: no
args.meaning: multiple-excitation zone number, the same index as ME <no>

args.name: a1
args.meaning: first ratio of the line; a1 = 0 deletes the whole list of zone <no>

args.name: a2..a100
args.meaning: further ratios, one per SSI frequency in ascending order, |a| in [0, 10] (Error 118); with HOUSE <cmplxspec> = 1 the list is (Re, Im) pairs; lines append

ANALYS.summary: Sets the ANALYS module options. ANALYS forms the soil impedance and solves the SSI equations frequency by frequency for seismic or vibration loading, giving the transfer functions FILE8; options cover restarts, frequency source, control point and global impedance.
ANALYS.notes: Coherent/incoherent, wave passage and multiple excitation are set by HOUSE; FFL/FFM and Delete Restart Files by ANALYSX.

args.name: opmode
args.meaning: operation mode

values.1: data check only (inputs verified and echoed, nothing solved)

args.name: type
args.meaning: type of analysis; also used by MOTION and STRESS

values.0: seismic: load from SITE FILE1, FILE8 = acceleration transfer functions
values.1: foundation vibration: load from FORCE FILE9, FILE8 = displacement transfer functions

args.name: mode
args.meaning: analysis (restart) mode; codes are 0-based, the manual names them Mode 1, 2, 3

values.1: new structure (Mode 2): reuses the impedances COOX
values.2: new seismic environment (Mode 3): new FILE1, reuses COOX and COOTK
values.3: new dynamic loading (Mode 3): new FILE9, reuses COOX and COOTK

args.name: save
args.meaning: keep restart files COOXqqq (impedance) and COOTKqqq (factorized system) for later restart runs

args.name: prnt
args.meaning: transfer-function print option of the listing

values.0: real and imaginary parts, all 6 DOF per node

args.name: fopt
args.meaning: which frequencies are solved

values.1: every frequency stored in FILE1 (seismic) or FILE9 (vibration)

args.name: ang
args.meaning: coordinate transformation angle, deg, between the SITE x′ axis and global x (counter-clockwise about z); rotates the SITE control motion into model axes; range [0, 360)

args.name: xc
args.meaning: X of the control point: origin of the horizontal phase of inclined waves and wave passage, and reference point of the global impedance

args.name: yc
args.meaning: Y of the control point (same role as xc)

args.name: zc
args.meaning: Z of the control point; used only as the reference point of the global impedance

args.name: impe
args.meaning: global foundation impedance by rigid-body integration of the interaction-node impedances (3D only; files FOUNSTIF, FOUNDASH, FOUNDAMP, FOUNIMPD)

values.2: full 6x6 matrix

args.name: simul
args.meaning: number of simultaneous load cases solved with one factorization per frequency

values.0: single case: FILE1 (seismic) or FILE9 (vibration) -> FILE8
values.1: seismic: X, Y, Z cases FILE1X/Y/Z -> FILE8X/Y/Z (ang must be 0); vibration: single case
values.N: N ≥ 2: incoherent stochastic simulations (= HOUSEX <nsim>, max 50) -> FILE8001...; vibration: load cases FILE9001... -> FILE8001... (max 500)

ANALYSX.summary: SASSI-EDU extension carrying ANALYS dialog fields: how incoherency factors are applied (free-field load or free-field motion) and deletion of restart files.
ANALYSX.notes: WRITE emits it only when non-default.

args.name: ffm
args.meaning: application of the incoherency factors (D-INC-12)

args.name: delrst
args.meaning: delete the restart files after a successful restart run

AOPT.summary: Selects with 14 flags which modules CHECK checks and AFWRITE writes decks for (non-zero = included), like ticking the module boxes of the AFWRITE tab.
AOPT.notes: New-model default: SITE, POINT, HOUSE, ANALYS and MOTION on, the rest off (D-AFW-05); the two DEP slots must be 0.

args.name: equake
args.meaning: EQUAKE module (spectrum-compatible motion generation)

args.name: soil
args.meaning: SOIL module (equivalent-linear free-field site response)

args.name: dep1
args.meaning: LIQUEF slot: module not in this version; must be 0 (a non-zero value is ignored with a warning)

args.name: site
args.meaning: SITE module (layered free field)

args.name: point
args.meaning: POINT module (point-load far-field flexibility)

args.name: house
args.meaning: HOUSE module (structure and excavated-soil matrices)

args.name: dep2
args.meaning: PINT slot: module not in this version; must be 0 (a non-zero value is ignored with a warning)

args.name: force
args.meaning: FORCE module (load vectors for foundation vibration)

args.name: analys
args.meaning: ANALYS module (impedance and SSI solution)

args.name: combin
args.meaning: COMBIN (merge FILE81 and FILE82): no deck is written; the flag only makes CHECK verify that the files exist

args.name: motion
args.meaning: MOTION module (nodal histories, transfer functions, response spectra)

args.name: stress
args.meaning: STRESS module (element stresses and forces)

args.name: reldisp
args.meaning: RELDISP module (relative displacements)

args.name: panel
args.meaning: NONLINEAR module (Option NON nonlinear wall panels and springs, deck .eql); the manual text calls this flag PANEL

AVERAGE.summary: Creates line <dest> as the arithmetic mean of the source lines on the union of their abscissas, e.g. averaging ISRS from several input-motion sets.
AVERAGE.notes: All line math uses the union of the source abscissas with linear interpolation; outside its range a line is held at its first/last value (not zero-padded).

args.name: dest
args.meaning: line number receiving the result (may be one of the sources; an existing line is overwritten)

args.name: source1..source100
args.meaning: line numbers to average (up to 100); an undefined line is an error

AXES.summary: Sets grid lines and logarithmic axes of the active 2D plot (spectrum, time history or soil property), like ANSYS /GRID and /GROPT,LOGX / LOGY.
AXES.notes: Blank arguments keep the setting; with no plot open the values become defaults for new spectrum / time-history plots.

args.name: MaxTickX
args.meaning: thick grid lines at the major X ticks

args.name: MaxTickY
args.meaning: thick grid lines at the major Y ticks

args.name: MinTickX
args.meaning: thin grid lines at the minor X ticks ('Show Ticks')

args.name: MinTickY
args.meaning: thin grid lines at the minor Y ticks ('Show Ticks')

args.name: LogX
args.meaning: X axis scale

args.name: LogY
args.meaning: Y axis scale

BBC.summary: Defines backbone curve <num> by reading <points> X Y pairs (strain or displacement, force) from a text file, one pair per line, without the origin.
BBC.notes: Fewer pairs than <points> is an error and extra pairs are ignored; point 1 is the cracking point, whose slope Y1/X1 must equal the elastic stiffness (G·A of a panel, k of a spring).

args.name: num
args.meaning: backbone curve number (>= 1)

args.name: type
args.meaning: curve type, used for titles only

values.2: CMB, Cheng-Mertz bending

args.name: points
args.meaning: number of X Y pairs to read

args.name: yield
args.meaning: number (1-based) of the yield point

args.name: file
args.meaning: text file of X Y pairs (path relative to the working directory)

BBCGEN.summary: Generates the 22-point shear backbone curve of a wall panel (0 = all) from its ultimate shear V_u: cracking point, 20 points up to yield at 0.4 % shear strain, failure at 2 % strain and 1.02 V_u.
BBCGEN.notes: The curve (type 1 CMS, yield point 21, X = shear strain, Y = shear force) goes to the panel's BBC number, or the panel number when that is 0; yield strain 0.004 and shape are SASSI-EDU choices (D-NON-09).

args.name: Panel
args.meaning: panel number; 0 = all panels with the same inputs

args.name: ShearModel
args.meaning: equation for the ultimate shear V_u (as SHEAR)

values.2: Wood 1990

args.name: fc
args.meaning: concrete compressive strength f'c, ksi (British, gravity > 20) or kN/m2 (SI); must be > 0

args.name: fy
args.meaning: reinforcement yield strength, ksi (British, gravity > 20) or kN/m2 (SI)

args.name: Pn
args.meaning: web reinforcement ratio (fraction): ρH for ACI, ρV for the other models

args.name: Nu
args.meaning: axial force, kips or kN

args.name: bre
args.meaning: boundary-element reinforcement area A_BE, ft2 or m2 (Gulec-Whittaker only)

args.name: bys
args.meaning: boundary-element reinforcement yield stress f_y,BE (Gulec-Whittaker only)

args.name: CrackingForceLevel
args.meaning: 0: cracking shear V_cr = 3√f'c·A_w (ASCE 4-17); otherwise V_cr / V_u, allowed 0.10 to 0.50

BBCI.summary: Sets the yield-point number and the type of backbone curve <num> (argument order differs from BBC).

args.name: num
args.meaning: backbone curve number

args.name: yield
args.meaning: number (1-based) of the yield point along the curve; 0 = not set

args.name: type
args.meaning: curve type, used for titles only; 0 = not set

values.2: CMB, Cheng-Mertz bending

BBCP.summary: Sets one point (X, Y) of backbone curve <num>, as one row of the BBC grid of the NONLINEAR dialog.
BBCP.notes: SASSI-EDU: a point beyond npoints + 1 creates (0, 0) rows that must be defined before RUNNONLINEAR (spec: 1 <= point <= npoints).

args.name: num
args.meaning: backbone curve number

args.name: point
args.meaning: point number along the curve (1 = cracking point); number of points + 1 appends a point

args.name: X
args.meaning: strain or displacement of the point

args.name: Y
args.meaning: force of the point

BBCX.summary: Sets the X values (strain or displacement) of backbone curve <num>, together with its number of points and yield point; creates the curve if needed.
BBCX.notes: Point 1 is the cracking point (origin implied), whose slope Y1/X1 must equal the elastic stiffness (G·A of a panel, k of a spring); BBCY must give the same number of points.

args.name: num
args.meaning: backbone curve number

args.name: points
args.meaning: number of points (must equal the number of X values given)

args.name: yield
args.meaning: number (1-based) of the yield point

args.name: X1..Xn
args.meaning: X values in increasing order, origin not given (shear strain as a fraction for panels)

BBCY.summary: Sets the Y values (force or moment) of backbone curve <num>, together with its number of points and yield point; creates the curve if needed.
BBCY.notes: BBCX must give the same number of points; a different <yield> replaces the stored one with a warning.

args.name: num
args.meaning: backbone curve number

args.name: points
args.meaning: number of points (must equal the number of Y values given)

args.name: yield
args.meaning: number (1-based) of the yield point

args.name: Y1..Yn
args.meaning: Y values (force; kips or kN), origin not given

BROADEN.summary: Creates line <Dest>: the envelope of the source spectra, peak-broadened by ±Smooth2 % in frequency, with shallow valleys between peaks bridged (Smooth1 %), as for ISRS design spectra (ASCE 4 practice).
BROADEN.notes: Percent values (15 = 15 %); Smooth1 comes first though the order of operations is envelope, broaden, bridge; sources with fewer than 301 points give a warning.

args.name: Dest
args.meaning: line number receiving the result (may be one of the sources; an existing line is overwritten)

args.name: Smooth1
args.meaning: peak bridging, percent ('Peak Difference(%)'): a valley between adjacent peaks no deeper than Smooth1 % of the lower peak is filled; 0 = none

args.name: Smooth2
args.meaning: peak broadening, percent ('Broaden(%)'): each frequency point spread over f(1 - b) to f(1 + b), b = Smooth2/100; 0 <= Smooth2 < 100

args.name: source1..source100
args.meaning: spectra to envelope (up to 100); an undefined line is an error

CALCPAR.summary: Prints the area, centroid, moments of inertia and the six section resultants of the active cross-section model (from CSECT), like ANSYS SPOINT + FSUM on a section.
CALCPAR.notes: Order: Area, Xc, Yc, Zc, Ixx, Iyy, Ixy, Izz, Fx, Fy, Fz (tension +), Mx, My, Mz in local cut axes with origin at the area centroid.

args.name: nx
args.meaning: X component of the original cut-plane normal (global); local z = n

args.name: ny
args.meaning: Y component of the normal

args.name: nz
args.meaning: Z component of the normal

args.name: rx
args.meaning: X component of the 'right' vector defining local +x (projected onto the plane)

args.name: ry
args.meaning: Y component of the right vector

args.name: rz
args.meaning: Z component of the right vector

args.name: sysno
args.meaning: number under which the local cut system is stored; 0 or blank = not stored

args.name: verbose
args.meaning: output format

values.-1: table, one 'name = value' line per parameter
values.other: all 14 values on one line, no names

CALCSECTHIST.summary: Integrates the element-centre stresses of a cut over a section plane for every .ess stress frame of a list file, writing a CSV history of Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz with a final MAX row.
CALCSECTHIST.notes: Run it on the original model whose stresses the frames hold (not on a CSECT model); STRESS writes .ess frames with SECDATAOPT,1.

args.name: infile
args.meaning: list file of .ess stress frames: one header line (ignored), then one frame path per line

args.name: cutnum
args.meaning: cut of the active (original) model to integrate

args.name: px
args.meaning: X of a point on the section plane (global)

args.name: py
args.meaning: Y of a point on the section plane

args.name: pz
args.meaning: Z of a point on the section plane

args.name: nx
args.meaning: X component of the plane normal (global); local z = n

args.name: ny
args.meaning: Y component of the plane normal

args.name: nz
args.meaning: Z component of the plane normal

args.name: rx
args.meaning: X component of the 'right' vector defining local +x

args.name: ry
args.meaning: Y component of the right vector

args.name: rz
args.meaning: Z component of the right vector

args.name: sysno
args.meaning: number under which the local cut system is stored; 0 or blank = not stored

args.name: ts
args.meaning: time step between frames, s; 0 or blank: column 1 holds the frame position 1, 2, ...

args.name: outfile
args.meaning: output CSV: Time (or Step),Fx,Fy,Fz,Mx,My,Mz; last row MAX = largest absolute value, sign kept

CAPTUREPLOT.summary: Saves the active plot as an image file, like ANSYS /SHOW,PNG. Same as File > Export Image.
CAPTUREPLOT.notes: Error if no plot is open.

args.name: FileName
args.meaning: image file name (rest of the line): PNG when '.png' appears anywhere in the name, any case; otherwise BMP

CD.summary: Changes the working directory used for relative paths (MKDIR, MDL; input files are searched there after the model directory); like ANSYS /CWD.
CD.notes: The directory must exist; SASSI-EDU: CD with no argument prints the current working directory.

args.name: dir
args.meaning: directory, absolute or relative to the current working directory (blank: print the working directory)

CHECK.summary: Checks the model and the analysis options of the AOPT-enabled modules against the manual's Chapter 10 errors and warnings, exactly as AFWRITE would, and writes <model>.err when the model has a name and path.
CHECK.notes: Set the analysis options and AOPT first; fatal errors (no nodes, Error 42; no groups, Error 43) stop the check.

CLOSEPLOT.summary: Closes the active plot; the most recently opened remaining plot becomes active.
CLOSEPLOT.notes: Warning if no plot is open.

CMODFORM.summary: SASSI-EDU extension selecting the complex-modulus form that turns a hysteretic damping ratio β into a complex modulus, used consistently for soil and structure (SOIL, SITE, HOUSE).
CMODFORM.notes: Keep the default for production work; form 1 exists to reproduce benchmarks that use 1 + 2iβ.

args.name: form
args.meaning: complex-modulus form (D-CNV-03)

CNGVIEW.summary: Sets the view of the active 3D plot (rotations, pan, zoom), e.g. to show two plots from the same viewpoint; comparable to ANSYS /ANGLE and /DIST. Same as the toolbar Change View.
CNGVIEW.notes: Blank arguments keep the current value; with no plot open the values become the view of new 3D plots.

args.name: rX
args.meaning: rotation about the screen X axis, degrees

args.name: rY
args.meaning: rotation about the Y axis, degrees

args.name: rZ
args.meaning: rotation about the model Z axis, degrees (applied first)

args.name: px
args.meaning: horizontal pan, model length units along the screen right

args.name: py
args.meaning: vertical pan, model length units along the screen up

args.name: zoom
args.meaning: zoom factor > 0; 1 = fit the element-connected nodes

COMBXYZSTRAIN.summary: Runs COMB_XYZ_STRAIN: combines the effective strains of the X, Y and Z STRESS runs (directional FILE74 files) element by element by SRSS, with G and damping from the FILE73 curves.
COMBXYZSTRAIN.notes: File names are relative to the model directory; the inputs must come from the same iteration and HOUSE run.

args.name: FILE74x
args.meaning: FILE74 of the X-input STRESS run (blank = skipped)

args.name: FILE74y
args.meaning: FILE74 of the Y-input STRESS run (blank = skipped)

args.name: FILE74z
args.meaning: FILE74 of the Z-input STRESS run (blank = skipped)

args.name: out
args.meaning: combined output file

COMBXYZTHD.summary: Runs COMB_XYZ_THD: for each line 'outfile fileX fileY fileZ' of the control file, writes the time-step-by-time-step sum of the X, Y and Z relative-displacement histories.

args.name: inpfile
args.meaning: control file in the model directory: line 1 = number of lines n, then n lines 'outfile fileX fileY fileZ' ('-' = no file)

CORR.summary: Defines row <no> of the time-varying target correlation between the X and Y components that EQUAKE generates; used when EQUAKE <corr> = 1.
CORR.notes: SASSI-EDU (P1): ρ(t) is linear between rows and imposed on spectrum 2 in 2-s windows before re-matching, although the command prints a 'stored only' tier warning.

args.name: no
args.meaning: row (pair) number; giving the same number again overwrites the row

args.name: time
args.meaning: time of this point, s

args.name: val
args.meaning: target X-Y correlation coefficient at that time, |ρ| ≤ 1 (Error 94)

CPMODEL.summary: Copies the active model, name and directory included, into model number <Mdl>; the active model stays active and unchanged.
CPMODEL.notes: The copy keeps the same name and path, so give it its own MDL before AFWRITE, otherwise it overwrites the original's files.

args.name: Mdl
args.meaning: destination model number; must differ from the active model; an existing model there is overwritten (warning)

CRITFREQ.summary: Finds peaks of the interpolated transfer function (.TFI) that differ from the computed SSI values (.TFU) by more than tol percent and stores their frequency numbers in a variable, to add them as SSI frequencies.
CRITFREQ.notes: SASSI-EDU stores frequency numbers (round(f/df), usable directly in FREQ) rather than Hz values; the Hz values are printed.

args.name: tol
args.meaning: difference, in percent, between an interpolated peak and the larger computed value at the two bracketing SSI frequencies above which the peak is flagged

args.name: minfilter
args.meaning: percent below the global TFI maximum within which peaks are checked; lower peaks are ignored (0 to 100)

args.name: TF
args.meaning: transfer-function file written by MOTION, without the .TFU/.TFI extension (e.g. 00085TR_X); both files are read

args.name: Var
args.meaning: name of the variable that receives the flagged frequency numbers (redefined, counter reset to 0)

CSECT.summary: Builds in model <dest> the cross-section of the cut's elements with a plane, extruded to unit thickness along the normal, keeping group and element numbers and the stresses read by READSTR; then ACTM it and run CALCPAR.
CSECT.notes: Load the stresses with READSTR on the original model before CSECT; shell thickness is adjusted for shells oblique to the plane.

args.name: dest
args.meaning: model reference number receiving the section model (must differ from the active model)

args.name: cutnum
args.meaning: cut whose elements are sectioned (CUTADD / CUTVOL / SLICE)

args.name: px
args.meaning: X of a point on the section plane (global)

args.name: py
args.meaning: Y of a point on the section plane

args.name: pz
args.meaning: Z of a point on the section plane

args.name: nx
args.meaning: X component of the plane normal (normalised internally)

args.name: ny
args.meaning: Y component of the plane normal

args.name: nz
args.meaning: Z component of the plane normal

CSYS.summary: Activates coordinate system ns for the following node commands (N, NGEN, FILL, ...), like ANSYS CSYS; 0 is the global Cartesian system.
CSYS.notes: Nodes are stored in the system active when they are defined; AFWRITE converts them to global coordinates.

args.name: ns
args.meaning: number of a system defined by LOC or LOCAL, or 0 for the global system

CUTPLOT.summary: Opens a 3D wireframe plot of a model with the elements of a cut filled; the only plot that can show a model other than the active one.
CUTPLOT.notes: Without arguments the GUI opens Select Cut to Display; in batch mode that is an error.

args.name: Cut
args.meaning: cut number (CUTADD / CUTVOL / SLICE)

args.name: Model
args.meaning: model reference number; -1 = active model

D.summary: Fixes (val = 1) or frees (val = 0) degrees of freedom of nodes n1 to n2. Unlike ANSYS D, val is a fixity code, not a prescribed displacement value.
D.notes: val defaults to 0, so a D line without val frees the DOFs; masses and loads on fixed DOFs are ignored, and a fully fixed interaction node is CHECK Error 124.

args.name: n1
args.meaning: first node

args.name: n2
args.meaning: last node

args.name: inc
args.meaning: node-number step

args.name: val
args.meaning: fixity code applied to the listed DOFs

args.name: label1..label6
args.meaning: one to six DOF labels, global axes, set to val

DAMP.summary: Appends damping ratios to the response-spectrum damping list used for SOIL free-field spectra and MOTION in-structure response spectra; DAMP,0 clears the list.
DAMP.notes: Values are fractions (0.05 = 5 %), not percent; the list order sets the RS file suffix 01, 02, ...; MOTION expects at most 5 (more are computed with a warning).

args.name: d1
args.meaning: first damping ratio of the line (fraction); d1 = 0 deletes the whole list

args.name: d2..d10
args.meaning: further damping ratios (fractions, each in (0, 1), Error 72); zeros are skipped; repeated DAMP lines append

GTIT.summary: Gives group gr a descriptive title, shown in listings and output.

HOUSE.summary: Sets the HOUSE module options. HOUSE assembles the structure and excavated-soil matrices; this command sets the SSI gravity, ground elevation, 2D/3D, impedance method and the incoherency, wave-passage and multiple-excitation switches.

INCOH.summary: Sets the incoherent ground-motion parameters used by HOUSE: coherence parameters, directionality factor, embedded levels, number of incoherent modes, and the seeds and phase range of stochastic simulation.

INP.summary: Reads and executes the commands of a .pre file (written by hand or by WRITE), then returns to the command line, like ANSYS /INPUT.

INT.summary: Sets or clears a classification flag on nodes n1 to n2. Code 0 marks interaction nodes: the excavated-soil or foundation nodes where SASSI applies the soil impedance.

INTCOUNT.summary: Prints the number of interaction nodes, which mainly drives ANALYS run time, with an estimate of the memory ANALYS needs.

INTGEN.summary: Generates interaction nodes (the nodes where the soil impedance acts) for the chosen method: FV, FI (subtraction or modified subtraction), FFV or surface foundation; options 1-5 add to the existing interaction nodes, option 0 clears all.

RSTVIEW.summary: Resets the active 3D plot to the default view (isometric: rX -60°, rZ -45°), with zoom and pan fitting the element-connected nodes.

RUNANALYS.summary: Runs ANALYS: per SSI frequency it inverts the POINT flexibility into the soil impedance at the interaction nodes, adds the HOUSE matrices, applies the seismic (FILE1) or load (FILE9) vector and writes transfer functions of all DOFs (FILE8).

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

args.name: model

RUNHOUSE.summary: Runs HOUSE: forms the stiffness and mass matrices of the structure and of the excavated soil (FILE4 = <model>.N4, COOSK, COOSM) and, for incoherent or multiple-support input, FILE77.

args.name: model

values.DYNAMIC: time-history loads: APDL tables of the reference-frame acceleration (ACEL) and relative interface displacements

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

RUNNONLINEAR.summary: Writes <model>.eql from the EQL/P/S/BBC data and runs NONLINEAR (Option NON): nonlinear wall panels and springs are linearised from their RELDISP displacement histories, giving new stiffness and damping in <model>_new.hou.

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

args.name: model
args.meaning: number of the model in memory whose files are used; -1 or blank = the active model

values.2: z′ (vertical)

args.name: delt
args.meaning: time step Δt of the control motion, s (shared by all modules)

args.name: nft
args.meaning: number of Fourier components NFFT, a power of 2 (otherwise rounded, Warning 9); the Fourier period is NFFT·Δt

args.name: freq
args.meaning: frequency set number (FREQ) of the SSI analysis frequencies, shared by SITE, POINT, HOUSE, FORCE and ANALYS

SITEX.summary: SASSI-EDU extension carrying the SITE dialog's Linear/Non-Linear Soil choice: SITE uses the L-table soil properties, or the strain-compatible properties that SOIL saved in FILE88.
SITEX.notes: WRITE emits it only when non-default.

args.name: soilmode
args.meaning: soil properties used by SITE (D-SIT-06)

SLIST.summary: Lists local coordinate systems: origin, how each was defined (angles or nodes) and the local axis unit vectors.

args.name: s1
args.meaning: first system to list; blank lists all systems

args.name: s2
args.meaning: last system to list
args.default: s1; last system when s1 is blank

args.name: inc
args.meaning: system-number step

SOIL.summary: Sets the SOIL module options for the 1D equivalent-linear (SHAKE-type) free-field site response: history-file reading, SOIL gravity, outcrop or within input, iterations, effective-strain ratio and spectrum scaling.
SOIL.notes: Input direction, SOIL's own scaling, control layer and file are in SOILX; Δt and NFFT come from SITE; a final (format) token marks the legacy PREP form (Error 102).

args.name: nrval
args.meaning: number of acceleration values read from the history file; must be > 0 (Error 100)

args.name: grav
args.meaning: gravity for the SOIL free-field analysis, ft/s² (British) or m/s² (SI); independent of the HOUSE (SSI) gravity

args.name: header
args.meaning: number of header lines skipped at the start of the history file

args.name: outcrop
args.meaning: type of the input motion at the top of the control layer

args.name: save
args.meaning: save the strain-compatible soil properties to FILE88 (read by SITE when SITEX <soilmode> = 1)

args.name: iter
args.meaning: number of equivalent-linear iterations; 8 recommended, 0 for vertical input

args.name: ratio
args.meaning: effective (equivalent uniform) to maximum shear strain ratio, in (0, 1); 0.60-0.70 recommended

args.name: gravmult
args.meaning: multiplier on the response-spectrum ordinates (SA in g × gravmult)

args.name: cof
args.meaning: cut-off frequency: disabled, always the Nyquist frequency 1/(2Δt) (EDUOPT,SOILCUTOFF overrides it)

SOILPROPPLOT.summary: Plots the G/Gmax and damping curves versus shear strain (%) of a dynamic soil property (DYNP label) of the active model.
SOILPROPPLOT.notes: Without a name the GUI opens Select Dynamic Soil Property; in batch mode that is an error.

args.name: PropName
args.meaning: DYNP label of the soil property, case-sensitive (e.g. Sand); the rest of the line

SOILX.summary: SASSI-EDU extension carrying SOIL dialog fields: input direction, SOIL's own scaling of the input history, and an optional SOIL-only control layer and history file.
SOILX.notes: Exactly one of mult and max must be non-zero (Errors 77, 78); WRITE emits SOILX only when non-default.

args.name: indir
args.meaning: input direction

values.1: vertical: Vp, P-wave damping, no iterations (set SOIL <iter> = 0)

args.name: mult
args.meaning: multiplication factor of the SOIL input history (use with max = 0)

args.name: max
args.meaning: target peak acceleration of the SOIL input, g (use with mult = 0)

args.name: cl
args.meaning: SOIL control layer: sublayer whose top receives the input motion; 0 = SITE <cl>

args.name: file
args.meaning: SOIL input history file; blank = THFILE; rest of the line

SPECPLOT.summary: Opens a new spectrum plot of up to 50 line objects (like ANSYS POST26 PLVAR); later AXES, PLOTRANGE and title commands act on it. Same as Plot > Spectrum TFU-TFI.
SPECPLOT.notes: Without arguments the GUI opens the Line Selection dialog; in batch mode that is an error.

args.name: Line1..Line50
args.meaning: line numbers to plot; -1 ends the list (later numbers ignored); undefined numbers are ignored with a warning

SPRO.summary: Assigns to SOIL sublayer <layer> an L soil-layer property (thickness, unit weight, Vp, Vs, damping) and the label of its G/Gmax and damping curves (DYNP); the last SPRO sublayer is the half-space.
SPRO.notes: A sublayer without a label stays linear; the label of the half-space (last) sublayer is ignored.

args.name: layer
args.meaning: SOIL sublayer number, 1 = top, numbered downwards

args.name: prop
args.meaning: L layer property number of this sublayer

args.name: dynprop
args.meaning: label of the DYNP curves (case-sensitive; rest of the line); blank = linear sublayer

SRS.summary: Requests SOIL response spectra (absolute acceleration, one per DAMP ratio) at the top of sublayer <layer>, for the within or outcrop motion.

args.name: layer
args.meaning: SOIL sublayer number; spectra at its top (1 = ground surface)

args.name: save
args.meaning: save the response spectra (RSxxx_zz.RS, SA in g × SOIL <gravmult>)

args.name: outcrop
args.meaning: type of motion

SRSS.summary: Creates line <dest> as the square root of the sum of squares of the source lines, e.g. combining the ISRS of the X, Y and Z input directions.
SRSS.notes: The result is non-negative, so SRSS is meant for spectra and amplitudes, not signed histories.

args.name: dest
args.meaning: line number receiving the result (may be one of the sources; an existing line is overwritten)

args.name: source1..source100
args.meaning: line numbers to combine (up to 100); an undefined line is an error

SSAF.summary: Requests the spectral amplification factor RS(layer)/RS(layer2) between the tops of two SOIL sublayers, each as within or outcrop motion, for every DAMP ratio.

args.name: layer
args.meaning: first sublayer (numerator)

args.name: save
args.meaning: compute and save the amplification factor files

args.name: outcrop1
args.meaning: motion type at the first sublayer

args.name: outcrop2
args.meaning: motion type at the second sublayer

args.name: layer2
args.meaning: second sublayer (denominator); Error 109 if illegal

args.name: freqstep
args.meaning: frequency step of the output, Hz (values at k·freqstep); must be > 0 when save = 1 (Error 110)

args.name: title
args.meaning: title of the amplification output; rest of the line

SSTR.summary: Requests SOIL stress and strain output at the mid-height of sublayer <layer>, optionally with the histories SSxxx.TH (stress) and SNxxx.TH (strain).

args.name: layer
args.meaning: SOIL sublayer number; output at its mid-height

args.name: opt1
args.meaning: compute stresses

args.name: opt2
args.meaning: save the stress history SSxxx.TH

args.name: opt3
args.meaning: compute strains

args.name: opt4
args.meaning: save the strain history SNxxx.TH (strain in percent)

STATUS.summary: Lists the global model information: name, path and title, counts of nodes, elements and tables, gravity and units, MOPT, frequency sets, output lists, AOPT flags, symmetry planes and stored options.

STIPPLE.summary: Draws the lines of the active spectrum or time-history plot with distinct dash patterns, for black-and-white prints.

args.name: switch
args.meaning: dash patterns

STRESS.summary: Sets the STRESS module options. STRESS computes element stress, force and strain histories for the EOUT requests by interpolating element transfer functions and convolving them with the control motion.
STRESS.notes: Phase adjustment, smoothing, output step and post-processing flags are in STRESSX; the control-motion data are shared with MOTION.

args.name: opmode
args.meaning: operation mode

args.name: iter
args.meaning: compute strains in all soil elements automatically, for equivalent-linear nonlinear-soil SSI iterations

args.name: save
args.meaning: save stress time histories (.THS files) of the requested components

args.name: itran
args.meaning: write element transfer functions (.TFU computed, .TFI interpolated) for all element types

args.name: interopt
args.meaning: interpolation of the stress transfer functions, same schemes as MOTION <interp>

values.0: SASSI2000 dense overlapping windows, weighted averaging
values.2: dense overlapping windows, averaging

STRESSX.summary: SASSI-EDU extension carrying STRESS dialog fields: phase adjustment, smoothing, output step, and the all-element save and contour-frame (restart) options.
STRESSX.notes: WRITE emits it only when non-default.

args.name: pzadj
args.meaning: phase adjustment of the stress transfer functions, as MOTION <pzadj>

args.name: smo
args.meaning: smoothing parameter for interpolation options 0-5; 0 for coherent analysis, must be 0 with option 6

args.name: skip
args.meaning: output every k-th time step of the histories (0 or 1 = all steps)

args.name: savemax
args.meaning: save maxima in all elements (ELEMENT_CENTER_ABS_MAX_STRESSES.TXT)

args.name: saveth
args.meaning: save time histories in all elements

args.name: rstns
args.meaning: write nodal stress contour frames (NSTRESS folder, frames from Frames.txt)

args.name: rstsp
args.meaning: write soil pressure contour frames (SOILPRES folder, groups from Frames.txt)

SUBTRACTION.summary: Creates line <dest> = first source line minus all the other source lines, on the union of their abscissas.
SUBTRACTION.notes: All line math uses the union of the source abscissas with linear interpolation; outside its range a line is held at its first/last value (not zero-padded).

args.name: dest
args.meaning: line number receiving the result (may be one of the sources; an existing line is overwritten)

args.name: source1
args.meaning: line the others are subtracted from

args.name: source2..source100
args.meaning: line numbers subtracted from source1 (up to 99)

SYMM.summary: Defines symmetry plane (3D) or line (2D) <no> through two or three nodes, for symmetric or antisymmetric loading, so that only a half or quarter model is analysed; <node1> = 0 resets it.
SYMM.notes: 3D planes must be parallel to xz or yz and a 2D line parallel to z; incoherency, wave passage, multiple excitation and global impedance are refused with SYMM.

args.name: no
args.meaning: plane or line number, 1 or 2 (at most two)

args.name: type
args.meaning: loading with respect to the plane

args.name: node1
args.meaning: first node on the plane or line; 0 or blank resets plane <no>

args.name: node2
args.meaning: second node on the plane or line

args.name: node3
args.meaning: third node (3D plane; not collinear with the first two)

THFILE.summary: Names the control-motion acceleration history file (in g) shared by SOIL, MOTION, STRESS and RELDISP.
THFILE.notes: Format per MOTION <fopt> (default: first line Δt, then one value per line); SOIL skips SOIL <header> lines and reads <nrval> values.

args.name: file
args.meaning: path of the acceleration history (g); rest of the line; must exist (Error 73)

THICK.summary: Sets the thickness of SHELL or TSHELL elements e1 to e2 of the active group.
THICK.notes: E creates shells with thickness 0, so run THICK after the elements exist (EGEN copies the pattern thickness).

args.name: e1
args.meaning: first element of the active group

args.name: e2
args.meaning: last element

args.name: inc
args.meaning: element-number step

args.name: thick
args.meaning: shell thickness (length), > 0

THPLOT.summary: Opens a new time-history plot of up to 50 line objects (like ANSYS POST26 PLVAR). Same as Plot > Time History.
THPLOT.notes: Without arguments the GUI opens the Line Selection dialog; in batch mode that is an error.

args.name: Line1..Line50
args.meaning: line numbers to plot; -1 ends the list (later numbers ignored); undefined numbers are ignored with a warning

THTIT.summary: Sets the title of the control-motion acceleration history used by SOIL, MOTION, STRESS and RELDISP.

args.name: title
args.meaning: history title: the rest of the line, commas included

TIT.summary: Sets the model title, written to the module decks and listings; like ANSYS /TITLE.

args.name: title
args.meaning: model title: the rest of the line, commas included

TOPL.summary: Appends L-layer numbers to the free-field layer list above the half-space, topmost first; TOPL,0 clears the list. It defines the far-field soil column of SITE and the excavated-soil layers of HOUSE.
TOPL.notes: Embedded models: the embedment layers must appear in TOPL order with their own, not repeated, L numbers; at most 200 entries.

args.name: l1
args.meaning: L number of the topmost layer appended by this line; l1 = 0 deletes the whole list

args.name: l2..l200
args.meaning: further L numbers, downwards; identical layers may repeat an L number (not embedment layers); zeros are skipped

TPSD.summary: Names the target power spectral density file of spectrum <no> (two columns: frequency in Hz, PSD in cm²/s³ for SI or in²/s³ for British units), used when EQUAKE <tpsd> = 1.
TPSD.notes: SASSI-EDU also raises deficient PSD to the target during matching and counts the PSD check (≥ 80 % over 0.3-24 Hz) in the trial selection; the manual only reports it.

args.name: no
args.meaning: spectrum number (1-3), same index as RSIN, ACCOUT and ACCIN

args.name: file
args.meaning: target PSD file; a blank file name clears the entry

TRANSLATE.summary: Moves every node of the active model by (x, y, z); no other model data changes.
TRANSLATE.notes: The ground elevation is not shifted: check GROUNDELEV after a vertical move.

args.name: x
args.meaning: translation in global X (length units)

args.name: y
args.meaning: translation in global Y

args.name: z
args.meaning: translation in global Z

USED.summary: Fixes all six DOFs (as D,n,n,1,1,ALL) of every node not used by any element, so that stray nodes do not make the system singular.
USED.notes: Unused interaction nodes are reported, not fixed (fixing them would trip FIXEDINT); USED is the only model check that changes the model.

VAR.summary: Defines or redefines a variable: a list of text items (referenced as @Name[i], 1-based) with an integer counter reset to 0; loosely like APDL *DIM/*SET.
VAR.notes: Names are not case-sensitive; @Name gives the counter, @Name++ increments it, @Name[i] gives item i.

args.name: Name
args.meaning: variable name (letters, digits, underscore; not case-sensitive)

args.name: X1..Xn
args.meaning: list items, stored as text; the list may be empty (VAR,NNUM defines a counter-only variable)

VARLIST.summary: Lists all variables: the value of single-item variables, the item count of the others, and each counter.

VERIFY.summary: Runs SASSI-EDU verification problems and prints, for each check, the computed and reference values, the error, the tolerance and pass or fail.
VERIFY.notes: Work files go to a temporary folder that is kept only when a problem fails.

args.name: id|P0|P1|P2|ALL|LIST
args.meaning: which problems to run

values.id: one verification problem, e.g. VP-01 or 1
values.LIST: list the problems without running them

WALLFLR.summary: Separates shell walls and floors: deletes every non-shell element of the active model, puts each plane with at least 5 coplanar shells in its own group and the remaining shells in group 1.
WALLFLR.notes: Destructive: run it on a copy of the model (CPMODEL); group titles give the orientation (WALL along X / Y, FLOOR, OBLIQUE).

WAVE.summary: Defines the participation of one wave type (R, SV, P, SH or L) in the SITE free-field motion: field on or off, ratios at SITE frequencies 1 and 2, and incidence angle.
WAVE.notes: The ratios of all active waves must sum to 1 at each frequency (Error 55); without any WAVE command a vertical SV field (SH for <wopt> = 1) is used.

args.name: type
args.meaning: wave type; types 1-3 with SITE <wopt> = 0, types 4-5 with <wopt> = 1

values.2: SV

args.name: opt
args.meaning: wave field option

values.1: wave field (R and L: shortest-wavelength mode)
values.2: least-decay mode (R only)

args.name: ratio1
args.meaning: participation fraction at SITE <freq1>, 0 < r ≤ 1 (Error 54)

args.name: ratio2
args.meaning: participation fraction at SITE <freq2>; linear in between

args.name: angle
args.meaning: incidence angle, deg, between the propagation direction and the vertical z′ axis; 0 = vertically propagating

WELD.summary: Merges coincident nodes in the element connectivity, keeping the lowest node number, like ANSYS NUMMRG,NODE, except that the replaced nodes stay defined but unattached (remove them with RMVUNUSED).
WELD.notes: Masses, fixities and interaction flags are not transferred, and the two ends of zero-length springs (FIXROT, MERGESOIL) are not welded unless FORCE is given.

args.name: FORCE
args.meaning: SASSI-EDU: the word FORCE also collapses zero-length SPRING elements (FIXROT drilling springs, MERGESOIL interface springs)

WIREFRAME.summary: Switches the element plot between filled faces and wireframe.

args.name: Switch
args.meaning: wireframe mode

WPASS.summary: Sets the wave-passage and coherency-model data of incoherent HOUSE analysis: apparent horizontal velocity and direction of Line D, and the unlagged coherency model.
WPASS.notes: Active with HOUSE <wpass> = 1; SASSI-EDU refuses models 2 and 4 (coefficients not confirmed, D-INC-04).

args.name: appv
args.meaning: apparent horizontal velocity along Line D (length/s), > 0 (Error 113); 1.0e9 practically removes the wave-passage delay

args.name: ang
args.meaning: angle of Line D from the global X axis, deg; also orients the directional coherency models 2-7

args.name: cohf
args.meaning: unlagged coherency model (D-INC-01)

values.2: 1993 Abrahamson, all soils (not available)

WRITE.summary: Writes the whole model, analysis options included, as a .pre command file that INP can replay; the archive and exchange format between programs and versions.

args.name: file
args.meaning: name of the .pre file to write

args.name: path
args.meaning: directory of the file
args.default: model path (MDL), else the working directory

WRITESPEC.summary: Writes up to 50 line objects into one spectrum-format text file (one row per abscissa: x y1 y2 ...), all resampled on the union of their abscissas; READSPEC reads it back.
WRITESPEC.notes: SASSI-EDU: a # header line names the lines and values have 17 significant digits (spec: %14.6E, no header), so a READSPEC round trip is exact.

args.name: SpecFile
args.meaning: output file name (path relative to the working directory)

args.name: Num1..Num50
args.meaning: line numbers to write, one column each in this order (at most 50)

WRITETH.summary: Writes one line object as a one-column time history (dt on the first line, then one value per line), the ACS SASSI history format read by READTH with Pair 0.
WRITETH.notes: dt is taken from the first two points (x2 - x1); a warning is given if the step is not constant or the line does not start at t = 0.

args.name: THFile
args.meaning: output file name (path relative to the working directory)

args.name: Num
args.meaning: line number to write

XTITLE.summary: Sets the X-axis title of the active 2D plot (spectrum, time history or soil property), like ANSYS /AXLAB,X.
XTITLE.notes: With no plot open the title becomes a default for new spectrum / time-history plots.

args.name: label
args.meaning: axis title text: the rest of the line, commas included

YTITLE.summary: Sets the left Y-axis title of the active 2D plot (spectrum, time history or soil property), like ANSYS /AXLAB,Y.
YTITLE.notes: The right axis of the soil property plot is set with YTITLE2.

args.name: label
args.meaning: axis title text: the rest of the line, commas included
